extracted.intended_audience: readers of the book Operation Tailwind; military history enthusiasts, researchers, and veterans interested in SOG/Operation Tailwind
extracted.subtask_description: A site FAQ / companion page for the book Operation Tailwind that explains maps, message conventions, and answers contested factual questions about the mission (insertion/extraction points, ordnance dropped, force size, crash site, etc.). Meant to help readers and researchers interpret sources and resolve ambiguities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topographic map features and scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Topographic maps display natural and man-made physical features of an area and are shown to scale. This includes highways, roads, and trails, towns and villages, rivers, streams, and bodies of water, airfields, bridges, political boundaries, and notable buildings like temples and schools. There are also contour lines to depict elevations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grunts usually carried maps using a scale of 1:24,000 while helicopter pilots used 1:50,000 and fast movers normally had 1:250,000 maps. The elevation changes between contour lines are indicated in the map legend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate precision (4-, 6-, 8-digit grid coordinates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinates were given as four, six, or eight digits depending on how precise the sender wished to be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A four-digit coordinate identifies a 1,000-meter by 1,000-meter grid square; a six-digit coordinate gets within 100 meters of a point; an eight-digit coordinate is within ten meters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date-Time-Group (DTG) formatting and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Military message traffic always includes a date-time-group indicating the date and time a message was sent; it is found in the line above the 'To' line in the address and uses a twenty-four-hour clock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For standardization, messages usually use 'zulu time' (UTC). Example: '271139z SEP 70' = 1139z on 27 September 1970. Messages may also use local-time letters (e.g., '071133h Aug 70' means 1133h local = UTC+8 on 7 August 1970).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use photographic, airstrike, and LZ prep evidence to locate insertion/extraction points
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve conflicting accounts of insertion/extraction locations by cross-referencing pathfinder photos, Air Force records (such as LZ prep coordinates), and the locations of subsequent airstrikes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If books/documents disagree (e.g., next to Hwy 165 vs Hwy 966), favor contemporaneous photographic evidence and Air Force records showing LZ prep and airstrike coordinates; in this case those point toward the vicinity of Hwy 966 (LZ prep at YC 4370 0470 and airstrikes nearby).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciling conflicting eyewitness reports versus official records (tear gas/drop ordnance example)
rubrics_metrics.description: When pilot memories and written records conflict about actions (such as whether tear gas was dropped on the 13th, the 14th, or both), weigh pilot reports against formal Air Force mission records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider factors like weather (which can prevent ordnance delivery) and mission logs. Example: pilot accounts mention gas masks on both days, but Air Force data shows CBU-30 was dropped on 14 September at YC 4450 0380 and that on the 13th two A-1s were airborne but neither dropped ordnance—possibly due to weather.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimating force size from fragmentary records
rubrics_metrics.description: When official records are lacking for indigenous or mercenary forces, infer numbers from message traffic references (e.g., 'three platoons of Yards led by sixteen green berets') and secondary accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use logical inference (e.g., 120 Montagnards is divisible by three so author used 120), but account for casualties/wounded enroute who may not have disembarked. The author gives a working estimate (WAG) of 117–118 Montagnards on the ground plus sixteen Americans based on such reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locating crash sites by matching pilot photos to map points and reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine aircraft crash sites by comparing contemporaneous pilot photographs with mapped sites and after-action reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: photos taken by Woody Woodard compared to circled map sites and after-action reports led to identification of the CH-53 crash at YB 651 921; Persky made it about 20 klicks (12.5 miles) southeast of the extract site before going down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use correct operation name depending on archival source language
rubrics_metrics.description: Different parties may refer to the same operation by different names; choose the term that matches the archive you are searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All U.S. government correspondence refers to 'Operation Gauntlet' while Laotian sources call it 'Honorable Dragon'. Use 'Gauntlet' for American records and 'Honorable Dragon' for Laotian records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting policy-level documents to infer mission purpose (Tailwind as diversion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use interagency correspondence and high-level memos to determine the intended purpose of operations (e.g., whether Tailwind was conceived as a diversion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite contemporaneous messages and memos (e.g., a message from Amb. Godley to State asking MACSOG for a 'diversion' east of Chavane; a 5 Sept memo to CJCS that SOG was to provide a 'diversion' for CIA Operation Gauntlet) as documentary evidence of mission intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inferring extraction/resupply planning from COMBAT SPEAR messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Track COMBAT SPEAR resupply request and cancellation messages to infer whether an extraction was planned or the force was expected to remain in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a COMBAT SPEAR request (dtg 130930Z SEP 70) requested 3700 lbs to be dropped at YC 419035 at 141800Z SEP 70 (indicating no planned extraction), while a later message (dtg 140535Z SEP 70) requested cancellation of the resupply and indicated that the Hatchet Force would be extracted (with DZ 2.5 klicks west of extraction LZ).
